content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

- **§ 12.4 (p0050)** imposes on us — the Customer — a non-compete running through the term *and twenty-four months thereafter*, worldwide ("in any territory"), against "any product or service that competes with Vendor." The scope is undefined and it expressly bars acquisitions.
- This fails not only the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer) but also the fallback (named product, in-term only, ≤12 months, with development/acquisition carve-outs), and lands in walk-away territory on two counts: a 24-month post-term tail and undefined scope.
- It is also internally inconsistent with **§ 12.3 (p0049)**, where Vendor acknowledges we have made "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."
- Redline validated (ok:true): delete § 12.4, leaving § 12.3 to govern, with the narrowed fallback offered in the comment as a negotiating step.
- No double-flagging: the only other competition reference, § 24.2, restricts Vendor's assignment and operates in our favour.
